title: Charges of the basic particles
body: The elementary charge e is the magnitude of the charge of a single electron or proton and can be considered to be the smallest indivisible amount of charge.
ced_evidence: 10.1.A.1.iii: "The charge of an electron is −e, the charge of a proton is +e, and a neutron has no electric charge."
correction_note: product-owner-directed correction by the Claude session (David, 2026-10-10): the escalated row was corrected against its own CED evidence and re-checked by both independent checkers and the own-family veto

title: Uniform field and motion between plates
body: Between two charged parallel plates with uniformly distributed electric charge the field is constant in magnitude and direction, except near the edges of the plates, so a charged particle between them undergoes constant acceleration and its motion shares characteristics with projectile motion in the gravitational field near Earth's surface.
ced_evidence: 10.6.A.3 and 10.6.A.3.ii: "undergoes constant acceleration and therefore its motion shares characteristics with the projectile motion"
correction_note: product-owner-directed correction by the Claude session (David, 2026-10-10): the escalated row was corrected against its own CED evidence and re-checked by both independent checkers and the own-family veto

title: Change in the electric potential energy of the object-field system
caution: The energy belongs to the object-field system, not to the charge alone (10.7.A.1).
ced_evidence: 10.7.A.1: "the resulting change in the electric potential energy of the object-field system"
